label: verify-t2-patterns-deep

claims.claim: Chemotaxis along a self-made gradient of low-dose attractant with abundant carbon makes the E. coli soft-agar front faster than the Fisher-Kolmogorov front; speed rises with growth rate.
claims.source_says: This navigated range expansion process spreads faster and yields larger population gains than unguided expansion following the canonical Fisher-Kolmogorov dynamics. The measured expansion speeds follow a common increasing trend with the batch culture growth rate
claims.note: Both parts are in Cremer 2019 (PMC6883170), plus a summary sentence on low-dose attractant with an abundant carbon source.

claims.claim: Narla 2021 gives a closed-form speed for the GE model: proportional to sqrt(r) and sqrt(a0/a_m), independent of uptake rate; at chi0 = 0 it is the Fisher-KPP wave.
claims.source_says: First, there is a square root dependence on the growth rate r... further increased by the square root of the relative background attractant concentration... c does not depend on the specific rate of attractant uptake μ... In the absence of chemotaxis (χ0=0), the GE model reduces to F-KPP
claims.note: All four parts appear in the Narla 2021 full text (PMC8640786); I did not independently check the exact Eq 21 form.

claims.claim: The Patlak-Keller-Segel closure is not directly verified in agar and fails at high cell density in a channel; growth-rate dependence beyond sqrt(r) is the main open point.
claims.source_says: the PKS model has never been directly verified... While the model agreed well with our data at low cell densities, it diverged at high cell densities.
claims.note: Phan 2024 supports the unverified PKS closure and the high-density failure in a microchannel; the agar-specific and 'main open point about growth rate' parts are the agent's judgment, not in this source.

claims.claim: Law set 1.8.1 has no chemotactic-front law; fisher-kpp-speed (candidate, non-binding) gives only the lower bound c^2 >= 4 s D, and turing-ddi is not the right mechanism for a travelling front.
claims.source_says: it does not establish that a travelling wave exists, that compactly supported initial data converge to it, or that any population disperses diffusively. Constraint KPP1 relation: c^2 >= 4 s D; status candidate.
claims.note: The local law files and lawset-1.8.1 show both laws as candidate, KPP1 as a lower bound, and no chemotaxis or Keller-Segel law; turing-ddi's scope is a linear instability of a spatial mode, so the 'wrong mechanism' point is a reasonable reading.

overall: Three of the four key claims are supported by the sources as read. The fourth is partly supported: Phan 2024 says the PKS model was never directly verified and diverges at high density in a microchannel, but the agar-specific and 'main open point' parts are the agent's own judgment. The quote the agent cites for claim 2 covers only the a0/a_m part, but the other parts are in the same text.
